## `tuzy account`

Manage your account.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy account [command]

Available Commands:
  delete      Permanently delete your account

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)

Use "tuzy account [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `tuzy account delete`

Permanently delete your account.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy account delete [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy config`

Inspect and edit tuzy configuration.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy config [command]

Available Commands:
  add-token   Store a token (e.g. a CI or service token) after checking it with the server
  check       Validate the user config and a tuzy.toml
  edit        Open the user config (or --project tuzy.toml) in $EDITOR
  path        Print where configuration and credentials live

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)

Use "tuzy config [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `tuzy config add-token`

Stores a token in the OS keychain (or, with --file, the 0600 credentials file) after checking
it with the server. Pass "-" to read the token from stdin: a token on the command line ends up
in your shell history and is visible to other users in `ps`.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy config add-token <token | -> [flags]

Examples:
  echo "$TUZY_TOKEN" | tuzy config add-token -
  tuzy config add-token - --file < token.txt   # headless service

Flags:
      --file   store in the 0600 credentials file instead of the OS keychain (headless services)

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy config check`

Validate the user config and a tuzy.toml.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy config check [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --file string   project file to check (default "tuzy.toml")

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy config edit`

Open the user config (or --project tuzy.toml) in $EDITOR.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy config edit [flags]

Flags:
      --project   edit ./tuzy.toml instead

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy config path`

Print where configuration and credentials live.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy config path [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy http`

Expose a local HTTP service at a permanent https://<name>.tuzy.dev URL.
Without --name your default name is used (the first run asks you to pick one).

The target can be a port, host:port, http://, https:// (use --upstream-insecure for a self-signed
local app) or a file:// directory to serve (read-only, with directory listing; dotfiles hidden).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy http <port | host:port | http://host:port | https://host:port | file:///path> [flags]

Examples:
  tuzy http 3000
  tuzy http 3000 --name shop
  tuzy http 127.0.0.1:8080 --name api --host-header rewrite
  tuzy http https://localhost:8443 --upstream-insecure
  tuzy http file:///path/to/site

Flags:
      --force                 take over the name even if it is live on another device
      --host-header string    Host header sent to the local app: "preserve" (tunnel host) or "rewrite" (local target host) (default "preserve")
      --inspect-addr string   inspector address (default 127.0.0.1:4040)
      --log string            write structured logs to stdout, stderr or a file (false: off)
      --log-format string     log format: term, logfmt or json
      --log-level string      log level: debug, info, warn or error
      --name string           tunnel name (default: your default name)
      --no-inspect            don't start the local request inspector
  -q, --quiet                 don't print the access log
      --upstream-insecure     skip TLS certificate verification for an https:// upstream (prints a warning)
      --upstream-sni string   SNI sent to an https:// upstream; it also sets the name verified in the cert

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy login`

Log in with a 6-digit code sent to your email. The first login creates your account.
The token is stored in your OS keychain. For CI, create a token with `tuzy tokens create` and
set TUZY_TOKEN instead.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy login [flags]

Flags:
      --email string   your email address

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy logout`

Revoke this device's token and close its tunnels.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy logout [flags]

Flags:
      --local   only forget the token on this machine (e.g. when offline)

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy names`

Manage your permanent subdomains (up to 10).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy names [flags]
  tuzy names [command]

Available Commands:
  add         Reserve a name (no name: pick a random one); also reclaims a name you released
  default     Use this name when `tuzy http` has no --name
  ls          List your names
  rename      Rename a name (a running tunnel moves automatically)
  rm          Release a name (held for you for 12 months)

Flags:
      --json   print JSON
      --live   show whether each tunnel is online (default true)

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)

Use "tuzy names [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `tuzy names add`

Reserve a name (no name: pick a random one); also reclaims a name you released.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy names add [name] [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy names default`

Use this name when `tuzy http` has no --name.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy names default <name> [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy names ls`

List your names.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy names ls [flags]

Flags:
      --json   print JSON
      --live   show whether each tunnel is online (default true)

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy names rename`

Rename a name (a running tunnel moves automatically).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy names rename <old> <new> [flags]

Flags:
  -y, --yes   don't ask for confirmation

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy names rm`

Release a name (held for you for 12 months).

```text
Usage:

Flags:
  -y, --yes   don't ask for confirmation

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy service`

Installs a user-level service that runs every tunnel in a tuzy.toml at login and keeps it up:
a launchd agent on macOS, a systemd --user unit on Linux, a logon task on Windows.
Logs are JSON; `tuzy service status` prints where.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service [command]

Available Commands:
  install     Install the service (then `tuzy service start`)
  restart     Restart the service (after `tuzy update` or editing tuzy.toml)
  start       Start the service
  status      Show whether the service runs and where it logs
  stop        Stop the service (it starts again at next login)
  uninstall   Stop and remove the service

Flags:
  -f, --file string   project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)

Use "tuzy service [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `tuzy service install`

Install the service (then `tuzy service start`).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service install [flags]

Flags:
      --dry-run   print the unit/plist instead of installing

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

### `tuzy service restart`

Restart the service (after `tuzy update` or editing tuzy.toml).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service restart [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

### `tuzy service start`

Start the service.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service start [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

### `tuzy service status`

Show whether the service runs and where it logs.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service status [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

### `tuzy service stop`

Stop the service (it starts again at next login).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service stop [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

### `tuzy service uninstall`

Stop and remove the service.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy service uninstall [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
  -f, --file string     project file with the tunnels to run (default "tuzy.toml")
```

## `tuzy start`

Start tunnels defined in tuzy.toml.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy start [name…] | --all [flags]

Examples:
  # tuzy.toml
  [tunnels.web]
  addr = "3000"

  [tunnels.api]
  addr = "8080"
  host_header = "rewrite"

  tuzy start --all
  tuzy start web

Flags:
      --all                   start every tunnel in the file
  -f, --file string           project file (default "tuzy.toml")
      --force                 take over names that are live on another device
      --inspect-addr string   inspector address (default 127.0.0.1:4040)
      --log string            write structured logs to stdout, stderr or a file (false: off)
      --log-format string     log format: term, logfmt or json
      --log-level string      log level: debug, info, warn or error
      --no-inspect            don't start the local request inspector
  -q, --quiet                 don't print the access log

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy tokens`

Manage API tokens (e.g. for CI).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy tokens [command]

Available Commands:
  create      Create a token (default scope: connect, for CI)
  ls          List your active tokens
  rm          Revoke a token and close its tunnels

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)

Use "tuzy tokens [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### `tuzy tokens create`

Create a token (default scope: connect, for CI).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy tokens create [flags]

Examples:
  tuzy tokens create --label github-actions --expires 90d
  TUZY_TOKEN=<token> tuzy http 3000 --name preview

Flags:
      --expires string         absolute expiry in days, e.g. 90d (tokens also expire after 90 idle days)
      --label tuzy tokens ls   label shown in tuzy tokens ls (default "ci")
      --scope string           "connect" (open tunnels only) or "full" (default "connect")

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy tokens ls`

List your active tokens.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy tokens ls [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

### `tuzy tokens rm`

Revoke a token and close its tunnels.

```text
Usage:
  tuzy tokens rm <id> [flags]

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```

## `tuzy update`

Update tuzy to the latest release (verified download, atomic replace).

```text
Usage:
  tuzy update [flags]

Flags:
      --check            only report whether an update is available
      --version string   install this version (e.g. v1.2.3, also prereleases or downgrades)

Global Flags:
      --config string   user config file (default $UserConfigDir/tuzy/config.toml)
```
